tagline: Nine miles along an ancient beach ridge.
intro: The byway follows SR 254 east from Sheffield into Avon, on North Ridge Road and then Detroit Road, about 9 miles along the northernmost of the ancient beach ridges, past more than a hundred historic houses, the oldest going back to the 1830s. Avon was once called the Greenhouse Capital of America, and a few greenhouses are left.
The name took a while to settle. The township was organized in 1818 as Xeuma, was renamed Troy, and became Avon in 1824.

moments.title: Milton Garfield House
moments.text: Milton Garfield's Greek Revival house of 1839 was featured in I. T. Frary's Early Homes of Ohio, and in 1851 he and Tempe Garfield sold Sheffield an acre for a graveyard.

moments.title: Olde Avon Village
moments.text: Among old buildings, some moved here to escape demolition, sits the Rock of Avon, a granite boulder left by the glaciers and dated at two billion years.

moments.title: The Stone Eagle
moments.text: William Hurst's Greek Revival house, its details taken from Minard Lafever's pattern book, is counted among the finest stone houses in the Western Reserve.
